attribution.note: The sentence follows a quoted Wall Street Journal passage and carries an internal ellipsis, which marks a spliced quotation. The voice matches the quoted WSJ paragraphs before it. Zitron's own reply starts at 'And no, Microsoft...'. He agrees with the quoted words, but they appear not to be his own.

semantics.note: Read as a claim, the normalised proposition matches the quoted words. The problem is who wrote them, not what they say.

contract.note: Reading 'dominant' as a leading contributor to growth, and 'real revenues' as substantial realised sales, is ordinary. Limiting the scope to physical infrastructure is strict but follows the words.

evidence.note: St. Louis Fed analysis of the 2025 period. It combines software and R&D with equipment and construction, so it does not isolate the physical buildout.
Unverified report of OpenAI's realised revenue for H1 2025. One company's figure cannot settle a claim about the whole industry with no stated threshold.

reviews.rationale: The case text indicates the statement is a quotation from the WSJ, not Zitron's own words. Under policy, quoted material is not the subject's claim, so the case is misattributed. Even on the merits, the packet would leave the claim unresolved: e1 is too broad and e2 covers one company only.
reviews.abstain_reason: Misattributed: the statement appears to be a WSJ passage quoted by the subject (a spliced quote with an ellipsis, inside a quoted block), not words he wrote.

attribution.note: Zitron's own analysis in his own post.

semantics.note: Causal chain with an unhedged future consequence ('will thus make it less money'). The lock-in element is dropped from the proposition but kept in the contract.

contract.note: Reading 'less money' as revenue fits the surrounding talk of annualized revenue dropping. The undated revenue consequence correctly requires causal evidence, not later snapshots.

evidence.note: Cursor admits its June 2025 pricing change hurt trust. It does not tie the change to Anthropic's priority tiers or show any lost revenue.
Cursor says it passed $1B ARR in Nov 2025. This weighs against an absolute decline, but under the contract a revenue snapshot cannot decide the causal claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no verified Cursor contract, no evidence that Anthropic's revenue grew because of the pricing change, and no retention analysis. Customer dissatisfaction is partly shown, but the cause is not. Later ARR growth is context and cannot defeat an undated causal claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense claim about LLM economics. The 'justify the costs' part is evaluative but is given a commercial reading.

contract.note: The commercial provider-economics reading is ordinary. Restricting a general present-tense claim to Q2 2025 is a drafter's choice but reasonable for measurement.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1, filed before the evaluation date, shows a Q2 2025 operating loss and H1 revenue just above cost of revenue. That is one provider only, with no isolated scale effect.
Unverified report of OpenAI's H1 2025 cash burn. Cash burn is not a service-level profit measure.

reviews.rationale: Company-level losses at two providers fit the claim's tone. But the contract asks for representative service-level profitability and evidence that scale does not fix it, and the packet supplies neither. Anthropic's positive gross margin also complicates the picture.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Expect to see' is an unqualified expectation. The antecedent (the AI bubble popping and capex falling) comes correctly from the preceding paragraph.

contract.note: Requiring the bust to come first, and both trends to accelerate, is fair. Treating 'first time in living memory' as rhetoric is reasonable.

evidence.note: Challenger data shows 2026 tech job-cut announcements up 54% year over year. There is no established AI bust before it, no offshoring measure, and no causal link.
Cross-industry CFO survey on outsourcing plans. It does not cover tech-sector offshoring after a bust.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not establish the antecedent, an AI bust with a substantive capex decline, so the conditional forecast cannot be scored. Higher tech layoffs alone do not trigger or resolve it, and the forecast has no deadline.
